spouse.description: One spouse, none, or several -- Khadi, Meera and Mehme each have more than one.

reincarnation_of.description:
An earlier character this one is a later vessel of -- a rebirth, or a binding.

Two of the three uses are bindings rather than rebirths, which is worth knowing before reading the field's name too literally. Guyuk the Seed-Gleaner is genuinely reborn. Captain Varuna and Mitra are gods bound into mortal frames for the era the game is played in -- `deity_in_mortal_shell` is the species that says so, and this field says which deity.

Deliberately not a key under `relations`, which is kinship -- parents, siblings, spouse, children. A rebirth is not a relative; Guyuk the Seed-Gleaner is not descended from Guyuk the Storm-Bone Khan, she is her.

This exists because one character was a participant in events four epochs apart. `epoch` says when someone first appears rather than the only era they may act in, so that was legal and not wrong -- but a teenage steppe nomad standing in the era after the Shattering is a different claim from a guardian outliving one, and canon should say which it means. Two entities with a link between them says it; one entity in five events across four eras does not.

`lint_story.py` checks the target exists and sits in an earlier epoch: a rebirth that precedes its own life is the same error as an event edge running backwards through time.

sample.description:
Marks this entity as a retained test fixture rather than canon.

The Dragon's Spine episode -- an event, the king who fought it, the dragon, and the range it happened in -- was written to exercise the tooling and kept on purpose, because four entities spread across four folders is a genuinely useful thing to test against. It is not part of the story.

Marked on the entity rather than in a registry, so it is visible to anyone reading the file. `lint_story.py` enforces the isolation that makes it safe to keep: nothing that is not itself a sample may reference a sample, so the fixture cannot quietly become load-bearing.
